case_number: Miscellaneous Application No 1852 of 2019 in Criminal Appeal No 1101 of 2019
summary: The case addressed the need for creating a safe and barrier-free environment for recording evidence from vulnerable witnesses in criminal trials. The Court emphasized the importance of implementing infrastructure and procedural safeguards, expanding the definition of 'vulnerable witness' to include victims of sexual assault (regardless of age or gender), persons with mental illness or disabilities, threatened witnesses, and others as deemed appropriate. It issued directions under Article 142 of the Constitution to ensure all High Courts establish Vulnerable Witness Deposition Centres (VWDCs), adopt training programs, and coordinate with legal services authorities. The judgment builds upon prior rulings in Sakshi v Union of India and State of Maharashtra v Bandu @ Daulat, reinforcing constitutional dignity under Article 21.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 2(d), Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012
Sakshi v Union of India (2004) 5 SCC 518
State of Punjab v Gurmit Singh (1996) 2 SCC 384
State of Maharashtra v Bandu @ Daulat (2018) 11 SCC 163
Mahender Chawla v Union of India (2019) 14 SCC 615
final_judgment: Directions issued for the establishment of Vulnerable Witness Deposition Centres across all districts, adoption of uniform schemes by High Courts, creation of a national training committee, and mandatory funding and compliance reporting.
